sections.bio:
With over 20 years of experience in the IT industry, I bring a wealth of knowledge and versatility to the table. I began my career in 2005 and have been continuously evolving and expanding my skillset ever since. I started with Mainframes, AS400 and AIX, and then transitioned into virtualization technologies like VMware, RHV, and OpenStack. Over the years, I have gained expertise in cloud and hybrid environments, followed by Kubernetes, and finally landed in the blockchain industry.

Throughout my journey, I have taken on a variety of roles, starting with services and architecture, then moving into presales, and finally finding my passion in product marketing. In my role as a product marketer, I have been responsible for creating and executing go-to-market strategies, conducting market research to stay ahead of industry trends, and working closely with cross-functional teams. I have also had the opportunity to lead analyst briefings, showcasing my expertise and ability to effectively communicate the value of our products to a wider audience.

With a broad set of technical skills and a proven track record of accomplishments, I am confident in my ability to bring value to any organization. My expertise in cloud computing, virtualization, and blockchain technologies has been honed through hands-on experience, and my experience in product marketing has given me a strong understanding of customer needs and the ability to translate technical features into compelling value propositions.

When I am not working, I have a variety of interests that keep me engaged and fulfilled. I am an avid reader, always seeking new insights and knowledge to bring back to my professional life. I also enjoy building with legos, cooking up a storm in the kitchen, and staying active through running and other outdoor activities. Overall, I believe in balancing work and play, and strive to bring my best self to everything I do.

posts.text:
Earlier this year I went through a layoff. A few weeks later I was already back in motion, working again, building again.

Growth isn't something I turn on when things go wrong. It's a habit I keep running whether the year is good or bad. What helped me come out of that layoff strong was that I was already doing the work before it happened.

That's why I said yes to Hattie the PMM's  5-day Visible & Valued Challenge this week. Moments of change are exactly when visibility as a PMM matters most. New conversations, new people who haven't seen how I think yet, only what I ship.

My goal for these five days is simple: get sharper at showing my thinking, not just doing it quietly behind the scenes.

20+ years into this career, I'll still rebuild a positioning document from scratch if the strategy underneath it is wrong. I want more people to see that thinking, not just the final output.

Thanks to Hudson Jameson, Andrés Valero, Pedro Navarro Pérez, Alicia Katz, Camilo Molano Herrera,  Gulsah Yurdakul, Leon Stern, Mitch Eger, Shelby Kinney, Skylar Deahl, Kimron F., Diana Chimes, Tomás Mujica, Rebecca Hopwood Marco Podien Brian Seong and so many others who showed up for me through this stretch, in ways big and small, even when they didn't know it.

Doing the 5-day Visible & Valued PMM Challenge with Hattie the PMM. 

Day 3 down.
What an opportunity: amazing product, amazing leader Viktorija Sreiberg Pajarske and amazing founders… what else can you ask for????

You probably have a library of old videos sitting in one language, doing nothing for anyone who doesn't speak it. I tested this weekend whether AI translation is actually good enough to fix that.

I ran one of my product demo clips through Synthesia's Video Translator, English into Spanish. Same content, new audience, no reshoot, no voice actor.
The lip sync is what got me. Watch the mouth, not just the audio, and it still holds.

Setup takes minutes. Upload a clip or paste a YouTube link (this is what I did), pick the language, done.

One detail if you localize for Latin America: my Spanish is Castilian, from Spain. Synthesia's output defaults to a more neutral Spanish, which actually reaches a LatAm audience better than my own accent would.

The free plan is enough to judge quality. No downloads and a few things are locked, but the paid tiers are cheap enough that it's not a real blocker once you've seen the output.

I wrote up the full process, step by step, video link in the comments.

Comment ES if you want it sent to you the guide and connect with me.

Paid collaboration with @Synthesia.
This is one of the best post of actual marketers making real stuff I’ve ever read! Great job Leon Stern and Diana Chimes
